features.note: Facade signage, numbered auditorium thresholds, corridor markings, generic menu boards, and the overview reinforce the accepted multiplex grammar across the capture set.
Sala 3 shows repeated acoustic panels, aisle-edge markings, stepped seating silhouettes, and two clearly different abstract screen frames.
Lobby, concessions, and kitchen presets read as a continuous public sequence with generated menu variants, POS-like faces, counter equipment cues, and entrance wayfinding.

The dedicated RS-485 view provides readable TC, BUS A-D, and UC A-D ID evidence, but the complete-network and UG67 views do not present a fully readable, uncluttered TC300 to RS-485 to UC100 to LoRaWAN to UG67 to Ethernet/Internet to Niagara hierarchy. Several yellow direction markers look offset from or dominant over their links, and the large LoRaWAN dash blocks obscure the four-to-one relationship.
Opaque architectural presets and translucent engineering presets remain distinct; the corridor comparison also visibly proves that labels can be suppressed without removing the underlying scene.

important_features.note: People, doors, counters, seating, roof equipment, and small highlighted devices retain a coherent relative scale.
Bright facade and front-of-house areas transition to a darker carpeted corridor and auditorium, although the white architectural surfaces remain visually flat.
Roof ducts and most RS-485 trunks read as contained, but the UG67-area wireless markers and direction cues create local floating or crossing impressions.

defects: In the complete-network view, internal endpoint and media labels are too small and overlap the translucent building, so the canonical hierarchy cannot be read end to end at the saved preset.
The UG67 engineering view is crowded by oversized blue LoRaWAN dash blocks; the four UC100-to-UG67 relationships are not visually separable.
Yellow direction markers are not consistently centered on, tangent to, and subordinate in size to their owning paths, leaving several markers looking detached or floating.
The dedicated RS-485 view proves IDs, but that evidence is fragmented from the complete-network hierarchy rather than carried into a readable canonical chain.
corrections: Recompose the complete-network preset so TC300, RS-485, UC100, LoRaWAN, UG67, Ethernet/Internet, Niagara, and client endpoint labels are readable in canonical order without overlapping the building or one another.
Reduce and spatially separate the LoRaWAN dash or wave markers so four distinct UC100-to-UG67 links remain visible and subordinate to their endpoints.
Snap every direction marker to its owning path centerline, rotate it tangent to link direction, and reduce its scale so it cannot read as detached geometry.
Preserve the dedicated RS-485 ID view, while carrying explicit RS-485 and UC100 naming into the complete-network view to connect the detailed proof to the end-to-end hierarchy.

mechanical.note: Blind surface review inspected saved pixels only; mechanical evidence remains gate-owned and was intentionally not inspected.
